data.title: Earnings Scorecard: 96% healthcare firms post EPS wins this week
data.description:
It was a major week for healthcare stocks, with 24 out of 60 companies reporting their results. Pharmaceutical heavyweights like Pfizer (PFE), Viatris (VTRS), and Moderna (MRNA) posted broadly positive quarterly results throughout the week.

The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) remained flat through the week even as the broader markets took a sharp plunge. In the year so far, the healthcare sector has risen more than 19% compared to a 7% rise in the S&P500 index.

Earnings Roundup

Of the 24 firms that reported earnings this week, 23, or 95.8%, posted better-than-expected EPS, while one missed analysts’ estimate. Notably, 21 firms (87.5%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.

On the revenue front, four firms lagged analysts’ consensus while 83.3% or 20 firms posted top lines above expectations. Notably, 18 firms (75%) posted Y/Y revenue growth.

Below is a snapshot of the quarterly print of some major firms in the healthcare sector:

Pfizer (PFE) posted earnings marginally above Wall Street’s estimates at $0.87 per share on revenue of $16.58B, amid less demand for its COVID-19 products. However, the company raised its full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance to a range of $2.95 to $3.05 and hiked the revenue outlook to the range of $62B to $64B. Concurrently, Pfizer also appointed Cecile Guegan as its next chief financial officer and executive vice president.

Viatris (VTRS) posted a mixed performance for Q3 2026 on Thursday, falling short of consensus for revenue while beating earnings guidance as its generics sales for the quarter fell for the first time this year. EPS rose 6% YoY to $0.71 even as revenue remained flat at $3.7B, compared to the prior year. Citing the strong YTD performance, Viatris raised its full-year guidance ranges for revenue and adjusted EPS to $14.70B - $14.90B and $2.56 - $2.63, respectively.

Moderna (MRNA) shares bounced back after days of decline after the firm posted better-than-expected Q3 2026 results and lifted its full-year growth outlook, citing higher COVID vaccine sales in its overseas markets. It reported earnings of $0.38 per share for the quarter on revenue of $1.3B. Speaking about its cancer vaccine, Moderna said it remains on track to submit regulatory filings for intismeran autogene developed with Merck (MRK) and initiate its commercial launch, subject to regulatory approval.

Out of the pharma companies that reported earnings this week, three were biotechnology firms, and three were pharmaceutical companies. Seven of those belonged to the health care equipment industry, and another seven to the health care providers & services industry, while four came from life sciences tools & services.

Upcoming Earnings

With the earnings season drawing to a close, only one major healthcare firm, Hims & Hers Health (HIMS), is due to report its results next week.

data.title: J&J posts late-stage trial win for plaque psoriasis pill in psoriatic arthritis
data.description:
Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) announced on Saturday that Icotyde, its FDA-approved therapy marketed with Protagonist Therapeutics (PTGX) for plaque psoriasis, succeeded in a late-stage trial for psoriatic arthritis.

With studies showing that up to 30% of patients with plaque PsO also develop PsA, the positive outcome of the company’s Phase 3 ICONIC-PsA 1 represents another medical use for the interleukin-23 receptor antagonist.

In March, the FDA licensed Icotyde for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in those aged 12 years and older at a time when additional trials, including ICONIC-PsA 1 for the once-daily pill, were ongoing.

At a rheumatology event on Saturday, J&J (JNJ) said that ICONIC-PsA 1 met its primary endpoint, with 58% of patients on Icotyde at Week 16 achieving an American College of Rheumatology 20 (ACR20) response, which indicates 20% or more improvement in disease activity.

In comparison, 41% on placebo achieved ACR20. 29% and 13% also achieved ACR50 and ACR70, indicating ≥50% and ≥70% improvement, respectively, compared with 16% and 5% over the same period.

There were no new safety signals associated with Icotyde, with the treatment showing a tolerability profile consistent with its established safety profile, according to J&J (JNJ). The randomized trial enrolled biologic-naïve adults with active psoriatic arthritis.

"These new findings underscore the potential of ICOTYDE to meaningfully improve outcomes in psoriatic arthritis and add to the growing body of evidence across psoriatic disease,” said David Lee, JNJ’s Global Immunology Therapeutic Area Head.

data.title: S&P 500 Consumer Discretionary Earnings: 89% beat EPS estimates this week
data.description:
S&P 500 consumer discretionary (XLY) companies delivered a largely positive earnings performance this week, with the majority beating analyst expectations on both earnings and revenue. However, year-over-year growth was more mixed, with six of the nine reporting companies posting increases in both EPS and sales.

S&P 500 Consumer Discretionary Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line: Of the nine companies reporting this week, eight (89%) exceeded EPS expectations, while one fell short. Notably, six firms (67%) posted year-over-year EPS growth.

Top Line: Of the nine companies reporting, seven (78%) exceeded revenue expectations, while two (22%) missed analyst estimates. Notably, six firms (67%) reported year-over-year revenue growth.

Here’s a look at some of the consumer discretionary firms that reported earnings this week:

Airbnb (ABNB) beat on both the top- and bottom-line with 19% revenue growth and a profit of $3.16 per share coming in better than Wall Street expected. Gross booking value rose 21% to an above consensus $27.7B, while the average daily rate for a booking increased by 4% to $179, exceeding $177.14 estimates. Third quarter adjusted EBITDA improved by 19% to an above-consensus $2.5B.

Booking (BKNG) reported an adjusted profit of $4.66 per share, up 17% year-over-year and 17 cents above expectations. Revenue was adjusted by $900M related to a matter associated with the Federal Trade Commission. Excluding this impact, revenue increased 9% to $9.8B, beating the consensus estimate of $9.54B.

Wynn Resorts (WYNN) reported a below consensus adjusted EPS of $0.33, with revenue falling 7.7% to $1.69B, which also missed estimates by $60M.

Yum! Brands (YUM) reported third-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.56, which was above the $1.51 Bloomberg consensus. Revenue was $2.06B, compared with the $2.07B estimate. Growth at KFC helped offset weaker comparable sales at Taco Bell. KFC recorded 1% comparable-sales growth and a 6% increase in system sales excluding currency effects. Its reported operating profit rose 9% to $425M. Taco Bell's comparable sales fell 4%, and system sales declined 2%.

Consumer Discretionary ETFs: (XLY), (VCR), (FXD), (FDIS), (RSPD), and (RXI).

data.title: Financials Earnings Scorecard: 87% beat EPS estimates; Y/Y earnings growth mixed
data.description:
Financial stocks took center stage this week as investors digested a wave of third-quarter earnings from major sector leaders.

The Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) continues to lag the broader market, posting a 4.57% year-to-date gain against a 7.43% rally for the S&P 500 Index.

Across this week’s earnings roundup, 15 financial companies reported results, delivering a strong beat rate against Wall Street expectations for both top- and bottom-line figures. However, Y/Y results were more mixed, as profit growth generally lagged revenue expansion across the group.

Financial Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line: Of the 15 financial companies with analyst estimates, 13 beat non-GAAP EPS estimates, one missed and one came in line, resulting in an 86.7% beat rate. On a Y/Y basis, across all 16 companies, nine (56.3%) reported Y/Y EPS growth.

Top Line: Of the 15 financial companies, 11 beat revenue expectations and four missed, resulting in a 73.3% beat rate. On a Y/Y basis, 13 of the 16 companies (81.3%) reported revenue growth. Loews (L), which had no analyst consensus estimates, was excluded from the beat-rate calculation.

Let’s take a look at some financial sector companies that reported earnings this week:

Block (XYZ) reported non-GAAP EPS of $1.13, beating estimates by $0.10, while revenue rose 10% Y/Y to $6.72B, topping expectations by $120M. Growth was supported by a 22% increase in gross profit to $3.24B, with Square gross profit up 14%. Adjusted operating income surged 92% to $923M. Management raised its 2026 outlook and expects at least 15% gross profit growth in 2027.

Allstate (ALL) posted non-GAAP EPS of $9.76, beating estimates by $2.80, while revenue increased 0.6% Y/Y to $17.35B but missed forecasts by $110M. Its Property-Liability combined ratio was 86.6%, with higher catastrophe losses adding 7.1 percentage points. The insurer returned $1.5B to shareholders during the quarter and said it plans to launch sales-related AI capabilities in early 2027.

Prudential Financial (PRU) reported non-GAAP EPS of $3.77, beating estimates by $0.45, while revenue declined 16.9% Y/Y to $13.49B, missing forecasts by $672M. AUM remained broadly stable at $1.616T, compared with $1.612T in the prior-year quarter.

Fiserv (FISV) delivered non-GAAP EPS of $1.75, beating estimates by $0.04, while revenue fell 1.4% Y/Y to $4.85B but topped expectations. Organic revenue was flat, with Merchant Solutions down 2% and Financial Solutions up 2%.

CEO Takis Georgakopoulos said revenue had stabilized after the second-quarter trough and expected Merchant revenue to return to growth in the fourth quarter. Fiserv also reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.20–$7.40.

American International Group (AIG) posted non-GAAP EPS of $2.06, beating estimates by $0.18, while revenue increased 17.2% Y/Y to $7.44B, exceeding expectations by $28.9M. The firm returned $787M to shareholders, including $527M in buybacks, and expected the full-year 2026 General Insurance expense ratio to be approximately 30.5%.

Aflac (AFL) reported EPS of $2.43, beating estimates by $0.63, while revenue fell 2.6% Y/Y to $4.30B but topped expectations by $90M. EPS declined 2.4% from a year earlier, indicating that the earnings beat did not translate into Y/Y growth.

MetLife (MET) delivered non-GAAP EPS of $2.78, beating estimates by $0.01, while revenue rose 11.2% Y/Y to $19.91B but missed estimates by $63.7M. Adjusted EPS increased 22% to $2.85, supported in part by $720M in variable investment income. CEO Michel Khalaf called it the company's highest adjusted EPS quarter.

Other Financial Companies

The remaining companies also posted mostly positive results. Assurant (AIZ), Franklin Resources (BEN), Corpay (CPAY), Fidelity National Information Services (FIS), and Jack Henry & Associates (JKHY) beat both EPS and revenue estimates.

Meanwhile, Global Payments (GPN) met EPS expectations and narrowly beat revenue estimates by approximately $267K, while Apollo Global Management (APO) missed EPS expectations but exceeded revenue forecasts.

Loews (L) reported EPS of $1.50 and revenue of $4.76B; compared with the prior-year period, EPS fell 38.3% while revenue increased 1.9% Y/Y.

Overall, the sector's results showed stronger revenue growth than earnings growth.

Earnings ahead: Investors will watch KKR & Co. (KKR), which is scheduled to report its results next week.

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: AMD, Qualcomm and Lumentum in focus
data.description:
The tech sector remained in the spotlight this week amid a persistent sell-off from investors and earnings reports from companies including Qualcomm and AMD.

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) closed in the green on Friday, leading a recovery from its worst day in more than a year. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

Fiserv (FISV) +25.71%

First Solar (FSLR) +15.33%

Corpay (CPAY) +13.47%

Block (XYZ) +12.16%

Jack Henry & Associates (JKHY) +7.37%

Top Losers:

Lumentum (LITE) -35.94%

Seagate Technology (STX) -28.48%

Marvell Technology (MRVL) -28.11%

Western Digital (WDC) -27.95%

Sandisk (SNDK) -27.44%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

Qualcomm crash following Q4 results

Qualcomm (QCOM) shares plunged after its smartphone chip revenue tumbled 26% in the fourth quarter as rising memory prices weighed on handset demand.

The San Diego-based semiconductor offered mixed guidance that overshadowed results for the fiscal fourth quarter. For the period ending Sept. 27, Qualcomm said it earned an adjusted $2.17 per share as revenue fell 7% year-over-year to come in at $10.44B.

Wall Street analysts have lowered their price targets on the stock given margin pressures and continued Apple modem share losses as risks to its near-term outlook.

Marvell announces $115B all-stock deal for Lumentum

Following speculation that a deal could be announced soon, Marvell Technology (MRVL) disclosed that it intends to acquire Lumentum (LITE) in an all-stock deal. The deal puts an enterprise value of $115B on Lumentum, or roughly $1,132 per share. 

According to Bloomberg, before announcing the deal, CEOs of both Marvell and Lumentum asked Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang’s opinion on the proposed deal, following which Huang gave his blessing on the potential tie-up, as consolidation among crucial suppliers in the AI buildout could reduce bottlenecks.

AMD in focus after better-than-expected results, guidance

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) closed nearly 4% higher in extended trading on Tuesday as the semiconductor giant reported third-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's forecast. This also led to Wall Street praising the company's data center strength.

Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore said the company is taking advantage of stronger server market conditions and taking “meaningful” share from companies like Intel.

AMD also recorded a third-quarter charge of more than $1B tied to the performance-based stock warrants it issued to major AI customers OpenAI (OPENAI) and Meta Platforms (META). The chipmaker struck deals with OpenAI and Meta, agreeing to supply them chips in exchange for warrants that could let them buy up to 10% ​of AMD if it meets certain milestones.

However, the stock closed over 17% lower on Thursday following a broader tech sell-off.

Micron Technology plunges amid chip selloff, Taiwan plant halt

Micron Technology (MU) has suspended plans for a memory chip plant in Taiwan amid a prolonged labor dispute, raising uncertainty over a major production base for components used in artificial intelligence systems, Bloomberg reported.

Micron dropped more than 17% on Thursday amid a sweeping semiconductor and AI-stock selloff, with reports linking the broader weakness to investor concerns about political scrutiny potentially slowing data-center development and infrastructure spending.

In other news, Cisco (CSCO) was downgraded to Equal-Weight from Overweight at Morgan Stanley on Thursday, as the investment firm said concerns are growing ahead of the networking giant's earnings, set to be released on Nov. 12.

HP (HPQ) disclosed that it has appointed former GSK (GSK) CEO Emma Walmsley as its new CEO. Walmsley will take over for interim CEO Bruce Broussard, who has been in the top spot since February.

data.title: 5 out of 6 communications services stocks deliver EPS wins this week: Earnings Scorecard
data.description:
Communications services stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major names, including Charter Communications (CHTR) and Fox (FOX).

The communications services sector (XLC) lost over 11% so far this year, compared to the 7% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

In this week's earnings recap, six tickers reported results, five (83%) of which reported earnings beats. On the revenue side, five companies exceeded revenue expectations, while one company trailed estimates.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Shares of Fox (FOX) closed over 6% higher on Tuesday after the media company reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 results that topped estimates, as the FIFA Men's World Cup, political advertising, and digital growth lifted revenue. Revenue for the quarter increased 22% to $4.57 billion, beating the $4.32 billion consensus estimate, while adjusted EPS was $2.54, above the $2.01 estimate.

Charter Communications (CHTR), meanwhile, reported wider internet customer losses in the third quarter, underscoring the pressure on its broadband business even as it laid out a new operating model aimed at returning to customer growth and cutting costs. The company lost 233,000 internet customers on a pro forma basis in the quarter, compared with a decline of 171,000 a year earlier. Revenue rose 9.1% to $14.92 billion, exceeding the $13.74 billion consensus estimate, while adjusted EBITDA increased 6.9% to $5.94 billion, above the $5.86 billion estimate.

AppLovin (APP) shares surged after the advertising technology company reported third-quarter results that topped Bloomberg estimates and issued fourth-quarter guidance above expectations. The company posted revenue of $2.18 billion, up 55% year-over-year, beating the Bloomberg consensus estimate of $2.07 billion. Diluted EPS came in at $4.30, compared with expectations of $4.04.

For the upcoming week, Take Two Interactive Software (TTWO) is one important communication services name that is scheduled to report quarterly results.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway, Mastercard, Visa among gainers; Goldman Sachs in losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street's major indexes went from cheerful optimism after the 2026 midterm elections to experiencing their worst day in over a year and a half. All three major indexes saw severe week-to-date losses from an ongoing technology selloff and policy fears related to AI.

However, the State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) added 1.15% week-over-week to close at $57.16.

United States 10-Year Bond Yield (US10Y) slid to 4.87% from 4.93% during the course of the week. Lower long-term rates help banks by lowering the impact of accumulated other comprehensive income on deal marks, S&P Global Market Intelligence reported, citing an interview with StoneX Managing Director Brett Rabatin.

Meanwhile, insurance indexes remained in positive territory for the week.

Among megacap financial stocks, Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) (BRK.A) led the gainers, advancing 5.24% and 5.03% from the previous week to close at $570.89 and $856,612.00, respectively.

The stock was rising ahead of the company's scheduled Q3 earnings announcement. For the third quarter, the investing behemoth reported operating earnings of $12.7B (-5.8% Y/Y).

Mastercard (MA) and Visa (V) followed, adding 2.30% and 2.19% to $652.70 and $422.65, respectively.

With Democrats winning the midterm elections, the ideas President Trump endorsed, such as capping credit card interest at 10%, face stronger opposition. Credit card stocks stand to benefit.

Goldman Sachs Group (GS) (-3.21% W/W to $865.82) and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial (MUFG) (-2.74% W/W to $20.97) led the weekly losers in the category.

Bank stocks fell but outperformed broader markets during the week, the worst week of the year for the market, according to a report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

The stock market rise in the morning after the election was partly a "relief rally" after a period of uncertainty. However, a reversal into negative territory reflected investors' belief that the war with Iran may last longer than expected, Stifel Chief Washington Policy Analyst Brian Gardner reportedly said. 

Truist Securities analysts reportedly said that they were "surprised that banks outperformed (albeit modestly) on the strong Blue Wave this week." The favorable regulatory backdrop for banks will last for at least two more years, but control of Congress does not actually move the needle for banks.

Life and health insurers Unum Group (UNM) (-15.79% W/W to $76.75) and Sun Life Financial (SLF) (-11.59% W/W to $71.53) led the largecap losers. The stocks lost out on the back of their quarterly results announcement.

Rocket Companies (RKT) (+17.66% W/W to $15.06) led the gainers in the category. Democratic sweep gave a boost to most housing-related stocks.

Among midcap stocks, Riot Platforms (RIOT) (+30.44% W/W to $16.71) was the top winner. The stock jumped as the crypto miner and data center operator reported third-quarter earnings above analyst estimates and its largest lease in history.

Ethos Technologies (LIFE) (-22.77% W/W to $33.51) topped the losers as the tech rout spread into insurtech. The Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) suffered its steepest one-day decline in 19 months on Thursday, confirming a correction and ending in a fourth consecutive weekly loss.

Another stock endorsed by the Trump administration and a crypto treasury firm, Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR) (-19.94% W/W to $8.82), was the next major loser in the category. Additionally, the week saw the company report its first-quarter fiscal earnings.

PRA Group (PRAA) (-33.71% W/W to $12.92), Evernorth (XRPN) (-25.49% W/W to $10.58), and LendingTree (TREE) (+32.46% W/W to $37.01) were the notable smallcap movers.

data.title: Coca-Cola files paperwork for India bottling unit’s IPO
data.description:
The parent company of Coca-Cola's (KO) Indian bottling unit, Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages, has filed draft papers for an initial public offering in India targeting roughly $1B in proceeds at a valuation of about $10B.

As part of the IPO, Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings will sell roughly 997.5M shares at a face value of Rs 10 each, marking an equity sale entirely ‌by its majority shareholder, Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte. Ltd., with no issuance of new shares.

Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings, which owns 60% of the company, will receive all the proceeds from the offering. The listing is expected to reduce its stake to about 45%, while Jubilant Beverages, which owns the remaining stake, is not selling shares and will have no change in ownership.

HCCH, through its subsidiary HCCB, functions as one of Coca-Cola's (KO) largest bottling partners in India, with its operations concentrated mainly across southern and western India.

data.title: Nutex outlines 3 to 5 hospitals per year growth, with 2 openings targeted in Q4 2026
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Nutex Health (NUTX) Q3 2026

Management view

  • “It was another strong quarter with solid financial results, steady collections, important reimbursement developments and continued growth in hospital volumes,” said (Chairman of the Board & CEO Thomas Vo), while pointing to nine-month volume growth and cash generation alongside year-over-year declines in reported revenue and adjusted EBITDA.
  • (CEO Vo) tied the year-over-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA declines primarily to prior-period revenue recognition effects, saying the declines “are not necessarily due to weaker collections in 2026,” and citing “uneven revenue recognition for the first 9 months in 2025” from updated collection estimates and the removal of “ineligible charts.”
  • (CEO Vo) highlighted reimbursement/legal developments under the No Surprises Act and IDR, including that “the District Court in Virginia reached a similar conclusion… bringing the number of states with provider favorable ruling on key IDR issues to at least 7,” and said Nutex “strongly support[s] the Murphy bill” while “firmly oppos[ing] the Pallone proposal.”
  • “For the remainder of 2026, our active development pipeline includes projects in San Antonio, Texas and Jacksonville, Florida, both of which are expected to open in the fourth quarter,” said (CEO Vo), adding that Nutex has “4 additional projects under active construction with expected completion in late 2027 and early 2028.”
  • “Total revenue for Q3 of '26 was $217.6 million compared to $267.8 million for the same period in '25,” said (Chief Financial Officer Jon Bates), attributing the decline largely to 2025’s revenue-per-visit uplift during early IDR realization.

Outlook

  • (CEO Vo) reiterated near-term facility timing, saying, “we have two opening this year, hopefully, before the end of the year, and that's San Antonio and Jacksonville,” and described four additional projects “hoping to open by the end of 2027 and a worst-case scenario beginning of 2028, depending on construction time.”
  • On cost cadence rather than formal guidance, (CFO Bates) said contract services should be “somewhere in that same type of range in relation to revenue, assuming everything else stays the same,” emphasizing the post-HaloMD renegotiation and CMS fee changes.
  • (President & Director Warren Hosseinion) set an expansion target for the Population Health platform, stating, “our goal is to build one to two new IPAs around our hospitals every year.”

Financial results

  • (CEO Vo) reported that for the first three quarters of 2026, “total revenue reached $644.9 million,” “adjusted EBITDA decreased 13%… to $211.4 million,” and “net income attributable to Nutex increased to $152.9 million.”
  • (CFO Bates) detailed Q3 profitability and margin, reporting “operating income… was $77.1 million,” “net income attributable to Nutex was $40.2 million,” and “adjusted EBITDA attributable to Nutex… $63.9 million.”
  • (CFO Bates) described volume and unit economics dynamics, including that hospital division visits rose to “54,622 visits in Q3 of '26,” and discussed IDR pipeline metrics: “approximately 50% to 60% are submitted through the IDR process,” “40% to 50%… resulting in an award determination,” and Nutex “has prevailed in over 80% of those terminations over the last nine months.”
  • (CFO Bates) emphasized liquidity and cash generation, reporting “cash… just under $250 million,” “accounts receivable… $356.1 million,” and “net cash from operating activities… $188.1 million” for the first nine months.

Q&A

  • Jeffrey Cohen, Ladenburg Thalmann: asked to confirm facility openings cadence; (CEO Vo) answered, “we have two opening this year… San Antonio and Jacksonville,” and “four that are under construction… hoping to open by the end of 2027… beginning of 2028.”
  • Jeffrey Cohen, Ladenburg Thalmann: asked about contract services directionally; (CFO Bates) said Nutex has not given “specific guidance,” but expects contract services to remain “somewhere in that same type of range in relation to revenue.”
  • Jeffrey Cohen, Ladenburg Thalmann: asked about noncontrolling interest; (CFO Bates) framed expectations as “somewhere in that high teens to maybe low 20% in relation to gross profit.”
  • Bill Sutherland, StoneX: asked whether revenue per visit under $4,000 is an appropriate range and about capital deployment; (CFO Bates) said “that range is certainly fair,” and on cash said the priority is “opening up facilities and hospitals,” while (CEO Vo) added “External growth, we're still targeting three to five hospitals per year.”
  • Yuan Zhi, B. Riley: asked if payers changed behavior post Fifth Circuit; (CEO Vo) said “payers are still paying,” while (CFO Bates) pointed to “a good solid nine months of cash collections.” Yuan Zhi also asked about policy risk; (CEO Vo) said, “we don't know,” emphasizing the legislative process.
  • Thomas McGovern, Maxim: asked whether lower CMS IDR fee increased provider engagement; (CFO Bates) said it “has slightly increased” but needs “a couple more quarters,” and (CEO Vo) added that the process still takes “four to six months” and “only 5% of providers like us actually do arbitration.” McGovern also asked about Nutex’s award-determination rate; (CFO Bates) said it “has been very consistent” and was added “just for some clarity.”
  • Benjamin Haynor, Lake Street: asked about IPA strategy; (CEO Vo) said, “having an IPA… surrounding your hospital is a great business development strategy,” and (President Hosseinion) added, “we're not trying to be the largest IPA… We're trying to essentially have primary care physician and specialist partners that are near our facilities.” Haynor also asked about physician vs. hospital collections; (CFO Bates) said “nothing material, but something that we're seeing.”
  • Eugene Mannheimer, Prime Executions: asked how many mature hospitals are profitable; (CEO Vo) answered, “the ones that are mature, yeah, I think all of them are profitable,” adding that “Two of those three are profitable already” for the three opened last year. Mannheimer also asked why fewer claims go to IDR; (CFO Bates) said payers are “paying slightly better on the front end.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive, with repeated focus on reimbursement sustainability, payer behavior, IDR mechanics, and capital allocation; questions pressed on “behavior change from payers,” revenue-per-visit range, and whether Nutex can provide “some guidance around 2027.”
  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more cautious/neutral in policy discussions, including (CEO Vo) saying “we don't know” on near-term policy change; management repeatedly emphasized monitoring trends “very, very closely” and highlighted cash and expansion priorities.
  • Compared with the prior quarter, management sounded more defensive/cautious around reimbursement/policy uncertainty (legislative proposals) while maintaining confidence on development timing and operational volume growth.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • The current call added a sharper legislative contrast, with (CEO Vo) stating Nutex “strongly support[s] the Murphy bill” and “firmly oppose[s] the Pallone proposal,” a more explicit policy framing than the prior quarter’s focus on final rules and court wins.
  • Openings expectations narrowed from Q2’s “West Little Rock, Arkansas; San Antonio, Texas; and Jacksonville, Florida… expected to open in the third and fourth quarter of 2026” to Q3’s emphasis on San Antonio and Jacksonville in Q4; West Little Rock was not discussed in the current call.
  • Q3 discussion placed more investor attention on revenue-per-visit normalization and the hospital vs. physician collections gap, which (CEO Vo) described as “slight differences,” while Q2 emphasized cost reductions tied to CMS fees and the HaloMD amendment.

Risks and concerns

  • (CEO Vo) flagged potential adverse legislative outcomes, saying the Pallone proposal “would eliminate the IDR process beginning in 2028,” and management described ongoing insurer practices and compliance issues as a key friction point.
  • (CEO Vo) noted “Physician fee collections are slightly down compared to hospital collection,” and said, “We are continuing to follow this trend closely.”
  • (CFO Bates) cited IDR process frictions that can prevent determinations, including payers providing “not accurate and complete data” and eligibility issues that cause claims to be “kicked back.”

Final takeaway

Management emphasized that Q3 reflected strong visit growth and cash generation alongside revenue and adjusted EBITDA comparisons affected by 2025 revenue-recognition dynamics, while reiterating two hospital openings targeted for Q4 2026 and a multi-project construction pipeline into 2027-2028. Leadership underscored continued reliance on the No Surprises Act/IDR framework for “fair market-based reimbursement,” framed material legislative divergence between the Murphy and Pallone proposals, and described capital deployment priorities centered on new facility development, infrastructure investment, and continued monitoring of physician-collection softness versus hospital collections.

data.title: Koppers forecasts 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $220M-$225M as pricing resets take effect in January 2027
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Koppers Holdings Inc. (KOP) Q3 2026

Management view

  • Chairman & CEO Leroy M. Ball said Q3 showed “underlying momentum in our portfolio” but also “near-term pressure created by continually rising input costs,” adding that “costs for coal tar, copper, diesel, freight, and other raw materials continue to rise and move through our businesses faster than we could recover them through pricing.”

  • Chairman & CEO Leroy Ball attributed resilience to Performance Chemicals and utility poles, saying “Performance Chemicals again delivered strong volume growth…driven by continued momentum in industrial applications and market share gains in our residential business,” while “utility and industrial products continue to benefit from a healthy infrastructure market for utility poles.”

  • Chairman & CEO Leroy Ball linked the earnings outlook revision to cost timing, stating, “That reduced our margins and led us to revise our earnings outlook for the remainder of 2026,” and added, “significant pricing actions will take effect in January 2027 and enable us to recover much of what we have absorbed this year.”

  • CFO & Treasurer Eric Brenner framed the quarter as margin pressure plus cash strength: “Sales increased despite a mixed demand environment…Second, higher raw material and logistics costs, along with lower crosstie pricing, pressured margins…Third, and importantly, we generated record year-to-date operating cash flow and record year-to-date free cash flow.”

Outlook

  • Management reduced full-year profitability targets, with Chairman & CEO Leroy Ball saying, “We revised our forecast lower to reflect higher input costs,” and guiding to 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $220 million to $225 million and 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.10 to $3.25 per share.

  • Chairman & CEO Leroy Ball guided to 2026 free cash flow of $115 million to $135 million, adding that it “has improved due to a $5 million reduction in expected capital expenditures for this year,” alongside total 2026 capital expenditures of “approximately $50 million.”

  • On timing of recovery, Chairman & CEO Leroy Ball said cost pressure would persist near-term: “The dynamic will continue to affect our results through the balance of the year,” while the reset was positioned for 2027: “about 80% of our current book of business is already agreed to for next year at prices that address the increases we are seeing across the board.”

Financial results

  • The company reported Q3 sales of $499 million and adjusted EBITDA of $58 million, with Chairman & CEO Leroy Ball saying results reflected “continually rising input costs,” and CFO & Treasurer Eric Brenner quantifying, “we estimate the year-over-year impact of higher input costs to be $16 million in the third quarter.”

  • CFO & Treasurer Eric Brenner reported profitability compression, stating adjusted EBITDA margin was “11.6% compared to 14.6% in the prior year quarter,” and that adjusted EPS was $0.77 compared with $1.21 in the prior-year quarter.

  • CFO & Treasurer Eric Brenner said cash generation remained a central highlight despite quarterly timing effects, reporting year-to-date operating cash flow of $127 million and year-to-date free cash flow of $92 million, while noting Q3 free cash flow of $19 million “due to timing of working capital items.”

  • CFO & Treasurer Eric Brenner updated leverage and liquidity, stating that as of September 30 the company had $360 million in available liquidity and $845 million of net debt, “representing a net leverage ratio of 3.7x,” and reiterated the “long-term goal of reducing net leverage to 2 to 3x.”

Q&A

  • Gary Prestopino, Barrington Research: Asked which segments would receive price increases and whether it was “across the board”; Chairman & CEO Ball said Performance Chemicals pricing was most advanced, noting “over 80% of our booked business, we have come to agreement with those customers…that will go into effect Jan 1,” while adding RPS would have smaller escalators and that CM&C was “a little bit uncertain.”

  • Gary Prestopino, Barrington Research: Asked whether the Florence plant was “idled or permanently closed”; Chairman & CEO Ball answered, “We are in the process of idling it…we have, at this point in time, not made a decision to permanently close it.”

  • Liam Burke, B. Riley: Pressed on Performance Chemicals share recovery and whether customers were returning; Chairman & CEO Ball said, “we did have a significant share loss…Heading into ’26, we were able to recover some of that,” and added “we have systematically grown our industrial market share over the past 3 to 4 years.”

  • Liam Burke, B. Riley: Asked if industrial was “moving the needle”; Chairman & CEO Ball said, “It’s not a needle mover…The industrial is helpful…but…we need a strong residential market.”

  • Liam Burke, B. Riley: Asked if RUPS margin decline reflected costs and Class I price concessions; Chairman & CEO Ball said it did, and CFO & Treasurer Brenner added it was “the deliberate price concessions that we made to secure volume…as we look to idle Florence.”

  • Michael Mathison, Sidoti: Asked whether lower capex was sustainable; Chairman & CEO Ball said, “my expectation is that $50 million would be the high watermark,” with “$40 million to $45 million” as ongoing needs “under our current portfolio.”

  • Michael Mathison, Sidoti: Asked if the buyback vs. debt paydown mix reflected priorities; Chairman & CEO Ball said, “our share price remains at a very attractive level,” and reiterated the intent to “reduce our leverage,” while adding the company continued to evaluate acquisitions “both in the UIP space as well as in the Performance Chemicals space.”

  • Garvit Bhandari, Singular Research: Asked about PC margin trajectory as copper hedges roll off; Chairman & CEO Ball said Q2 had “peak margins of roughly 22%,” Q3 was “roughly 18%,” and management expected “that to deteriorate a little bit further in the fourth quarter” ahead of 2027 pricing.

  • Garvit Bhandari, Singular Research: Asked whether the plan for PC plus RUPS to exceed 85% of sales by 2028 was organic or inorganic; Chairman & CEO Ball said, “we expect that to be primarily organic right now,” while adding, “if we are going to do anything on the inorganic side, it’s going to be in PC or UIP.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analyst tone was slightly negative to neutral, with questions concentrating on pricing recovery timing, margin durability (notably in PC and RUPS), and capital allocation trade-offs; several were probing but not adversarial (e.g., requests to “work through each of the segments” on price increases and whether capex levels were “the new normal”).

  • Management tone was slightly positive but defensive on near-term profitability, repeatedly emphasizing cost pressure and timing lags while expressing confidence in 2027 recovery; Chairman & CEO Ball said “we are not minimizing” margin pressure (via CFO Brenner) and added, “we’re extremely confident on the PC piece,” while describing CM&C as “a little bit uncertain.”

  • Versus the prior quarter, management’s language shifted from executing transformation amid volatility to explicitly acknowledging an earnings reset: in Q2, management said, “Our broader outlook for the business remains intact,” while in Q3 it said rising costs “led us to revise our earnings outlook for the remainder of 2026.”

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Guidance moved lower in Q3: Q2 guided 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $240 million to $250 million and adjusted EPS of $3.80 to $4.20, while Q3 guided adjusted EBITDA of $220 million to $225 million and adjusted EPS of $3.10 to $3.25, with Q3 attributing the change to “higher input costs…continue throughout Q4.”

  • The Stickney plan advanced from an accelerated end-of-distillation target in Q2 to completed shutdown milestones in Q3, with Chairman & CEO Ball stating, “we recently reached 2 important milestones by ending distillation activities on September 30 and then discontinuing the remaining chemical production at Stickney in October.”

  • Analyst focus evolved from Catalyst pacing and general cost pass-through questions in Q2 to detailed 2027 pricing mechanics by segment in Q3, alongside more granular debate about margin pressure tied to Class I rail concessions and PC raw material inflation.

Risks and concerns

  • Management highlighted ongoing inflation and lags in recovery, with Chairman & CEO Leroy Ball stating the company was “absorbing higher raw material, additive, and logistics costs today before we are able to fully recover them through pricing.”

  • CM&C volatility remained a key risk, with CFO & Treasurer Eric Brenner citing “conflict in the Middle East and safety-related coal mine closures in China,” plus operational disruption from “the receipt of poor-quality tar” and “transition and logistics costs” during the network shift.

  • Rail profitability risk was tied to pricing concessions and demand variability, with management acknowledging “price concessions that we made to secure future volumes have pressured margins in the near term,” while positioning cost actions including workforce reductions and the Florence wind-down.

Final takeaway

Management described Q3 as a mix of volume resilience and market-share gains in Performance Chemicals and utility poles, but with profitability hit by faster-moving coal tar, copper, freight, and other input costs that could not be fully recovered in 2026 timing. The company lowered 2026 adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS guidance, while reiterating that pricing resets taking effect in January 2027 and structural actions—most visibly the completed Stickney shutdown milestones and ongoing network optimization—are expected to support improved earnings and continued cash generation into 2027.
